function: Reason above_phy: the learned element is a GCNN branching policy that speeds up branch and bound for a user/target-to-BS task allocation and scheduling integer program (pp. 2, 3, 6, 10).
notes: Excluded as above_phy (Step 1, code 4). p. 3: "to indicate if the u-th user is associated with the b-th BS at the n-th time slot", and the same variable for BS-target sensing, so the decisions are user and target association to BSs per time slot (task allocation and scheduling; title: Efficient Task Allocation). p. 2: "via offline training so that efficient branching decisions can be made to accelerate the online solution finding". p. 6: "minimizing the final size of the branching tree" (reward of -1 per branching step), so the RL only picks the branching variable of branch and bound; p. 10: "the optimality of our solution can be guaranteed", so the learning changes the run time, not the allocation. The beamformers are not learned: p. 5: DFRC beamformer obtained "via beampattern synthesis" and Riemannian steepest gradient descent. Reported results (pp. 10-14, Figs. 3-10: interruption probability, sum rate, sensing success) compare only with non-learned schemes [8], [9]; the GCRL versus branch and bound run-time comparison is not in the main text (a supplementary file is mentioned on p. 1). Alternatives the reviewer may prefer: no_learning, because the learned brancher performs no physical-layer function and does not alter the optimal solution; or inclusion in area 5 if the DFRC waveform scheduling is read as an ISAC physical-layer resource decision, in which case the marks would be q1 0 (custom Bernoulli blockage simulator, pp. 4, 10), q2 0, q3 0 (no learned baseline in the main text), q4 1 (p. 10: complexity O(D n^3)), q5 0. Simulator is custom (Bernoulli LoS blockage, 30 GHz, 4 BSs, 16 antennas, 3 single-antenna users, 3 targets, p. 10).
